title: District thalassemia unit bank crosses 1,200 units in a single year
summary: A standing arrangement between eleven clubs and three hospitals turned an ad-hoc emergency network into a predictable monthly supply for paediatric thalassemia patients.
body: For years the district's thalassemia response was a phone tree. A parent would call a club president, who would post in a group, and somewhere between twenty and two hundred people would see it in time.
## What changed

Eleven clubs and three hospitals agreed a standing monthly roster instead. Each club owns two dates a year; the hospital confirms requirement seventy-two hours ahead; a shared sheet tracks donor eligibility windows so nobody is called before they can give again.
The result is boring, which is the point. Paediatric thalassemia patients need transfusions on a schedule, and a scheduled supply is worth more than a heroic one.
## The number that matters is not 1,214

It is 61% — the share of units that came from repeat donors. An emergency network recruits strangers forever; a programme grows a base. The clubs now measure themselves on repeat rate and treat total units as the output it is.
replicate: A named hospital coordinator per club
Seventy-two-hour confirmation window
Shared eligibility tracker so donors are not called early

title: Solar microgrid brings evening study hours to a tribal ashram school
summary: A 9kW rooftop array with battery backup replaced a diesel generator that ran for two hours a night, unlocking a supervised evening study block for 210 residential students.
body: The ashram school runs a residential programme for 210 students. Until this year its evenings ran on a diesel generator that ran two hours a night and cost more than the school's entire stationery budget.
## The install
A 9kW rooftop array with battery backup, sized against a week of metered consumption rather than a brochure figure. The club spent longer on the load survey than on the installation.
## What it unlocked
Three supervised study hours a night, every night, without a fuel line item. The warden reports that attendance in the residential wing has held through the monsoon for the first time in four years.
replicate: Meter the actual load before sizing
Budget for battery replacement in year five
Train two staff on basic fault-finding

title: Four gram panchayats take over water ATMs after a two-year handover
summary: The interesting part is not the installation — it is that all four units are now maintained on panchayat budget lines, two years after the club stepped back.
body: Installing a water ATM is a weekend. Keeping it running for two years is a project, and it is the part most clubs quietly lose.
## The handover was designed in from day one

Each of the four panchayats signed a maintenance commitment before installation, with a named operator, a card-based usage log and a monthly consumables budget line. The club funded upkeep for the first twelve months on a tapering scale, then stopped.
## Two years on

All four units are running on panchayat budget lines with no club money. One has already been through a filter replacement cycle without anybody calling us, which is the outcome we were actually after.
replicate: Written maintenance commitment before installation
Tapering funding rather than a cliff
A named operator, not a committee

title: Menstrual health curriculum reaches 38 municipal schools
summary: Co-designed with school counsellors and delivered by trained peer educators rather than visiting volunteers — a change that doubled session attendance.
body: The first version of this programme was delivered by visiting volunteers. Attendance was polite and low, and the follow-up questions never came.
## Peer educators changed the arithmetic

The club trained senior students as peer educators and moved the volunteers into a support role. Session attendance roughly doubled and, more usefully, students began asking questions after the session rather than during it.
## Co-design with counsellors
The curriculum was written with school counsellors rather than handed to them. That is slower by about six weeks and is the reason thirty-eight schools adopted it instead of three.
replicate: Train peer educators, don't parachute in speakers
Co-write with school counsellors
Measure post-session questions, not attendance alone

title: A three-year mangrove restoration audit, published in full
summary: Survival rates, species performance and the sites that failed — all of it public. The first district project to publish negative results alongside the headline number.
body: Three years after planting, the club published everything: survival by species, by site, by planting month — including the two sites where nothing survived at all.
## Why publish the failures

Because the failures carry the information. The two dead sites shared a characteristic — tidal exposure the survey had recorded and the planting plan had ignored — and that finding is worth more to the next club than the headline survival number.
## 62% at 36 months
Comparable published figures are scarce, which is itself the problem. The club has offered its raw dataset to any club willing to publish theirs on the same terms.
replicate: Publish species-level and site-level survival
Revisit at 12, 24 and 36 months
Record tidal exposure at survey, and act on it

title: Skill lab helps 140 women artisans move to direct online sales
summary: Photography, listing hygiene, pricing and GST basics — a six-week lab that ended with each artisan holding a live storefront and their first ten orders.
body: One hundred and forty women artisans, most selling through a middleman at a fixed rate, six weeks of evening sessions.
## What the lab actually taught
Photography on a phone, listing hygiene, honest pricing arithmetic and the GST basics needed to invoice. No branding workshops, no aspiration slides.
## Ending with a live storefront

Nobody graduated without a working listing and their first ten orders processed with a facilitator sitting beside them. The average income lift at six months was 31%, and the artisans who did best were the ones who kept photographing their own work rather than outsourcing it.
replicate: End the course with a live storefront, not a certificate
Teach invoicing, not branding
Sit with them through the first ten orders

title: Sanitation blocks handed over at nine zilla parishad schools
summary: Built to a shared district specification with a named maintenance owner per site, following the model that fixed the Anganwadi programme's durability problem.
body: Nine sanitation blocks across zilla parishad schools, built to a single district specification rather than nine local ones.
## Why a shared spec
Standardising the design meant spares are interchangeable, the same mason understands every site, and the maintenance instructions are one document instead of nine.
## A named owner per site

Following the model that fixed the Anganwadi durability problem, each block has a named maintenance owner at the school and a scheduled six-month revisit. The first revisit cycle is complete and all nine are functional.
replicate: One district specification, not per-site designs
Named maintenance owner at each school
Six-month revisit written into the handover

title: Two district Rotaractors selected for a peace fellowship exchange
summary: A twelve-week exchange focused on community mediation practice, with both fellows committing to run district-level training on return.
body: Two Rotaractors from the district were selected for a twelve-week community mediation exchange.
## The condition attached
Both fellows committed, in writing and before departure, to run district-level training on their return. A fellowship that ends at the airport is a holiday with paperwork.
## What comes back
The training runs across two weekends in the coming Rotary year and is open to any club in the zone.
replicate: Attach a return-training commitment before departure
Open the resulting training to the whole district

title: Cataract camp crosses 800 surgeries across three districts
summary: A pooled logistics model where four clubs share transport and post-op follow-up, cutting per-patient cost by a third against running the camps separately.
body: Four clubs used to run cataract camps separately, each arranging its own transport, its own surgeons and its own post-operative follow-up.
## Pooling the logistics, not the credit
The clubs kept their own camps and pooled only the expensive shared parts: vehicles, screening staff and the follow-up roster. Per-patient cost fell by roughly a third.
## Follow-up is the hard half

Eight hundred and twelve surgeries is the easy number to publish. The harder one is that 94% of patients completed their post-operative review, which only happened because the follow-up roster had a named caller per patient.
replicate: Pool transport and follow-up, keep camps local
One named caller per patient for post-op review

title: Library-in-a-box reaches its sixtieth village
summary: A rotating 300-book crate that moves between villages every quarter, tracked with a simple card system that villages run themselves.
body: A crate of three hundred books that moves between villages every quarter, tracked on index cards the village keeps itself.
## Deliberately low-tech
There is no app. A card per book, a register, and a volunteer librarian chosen by the village. Sixty villages have run it without a single support call.
## Sixty villages, eighteen thousand circulations
The crates are replaced on a three-year cycle. Losses run at about four percent a year, which the club has decided is the cost of a library people actually use.
replicate: Index cards beat an app at this scale
Let the village choose the librarian
Budget for 4% annual loss and stop worrying about it

title: Vocational programme places 46 hearing-impaired graduates
summary: Employer-side sensitisation turned out to matter more than candidate training — the placement rate tripled once the club started running sessions inside partner companies.
body: Forty-six placements across eleven employers, from a programme that spent its first year training candidates and placing almost nobody.
## The bottleneck was never the candidates

Graduates were job-ready well before employers were ready to hire them. The club moved its effort to running sensitisation sessions inside partner companies — interview adjustments, workplace communication, what an interpreter does and does not do.
## Placement rate tripled
Same candidate training, different audience. Eleven employers now have a written interview-adjustment protocol, which outlasts any individual placement.
replicate: Run sensitisation inside the employer, not the training centre
Get the interview-adjustment protocol in writing

title: Flood relief network moves 22 tonnes in 96 hours
summary: A pre-agreed roster of drivers, warehouses and verification volunteers, activated by a single message — built during peacetime, tested in a crisis.
body: Twenty-two tonnes of relief material moved through fourteen villages in ninety-six hours, on a network that was built when nothing was happening.
## Built in peacetime
A pre-agreed roster of drivers, warehouse space, and — the part most networks skip — verification volunteers whose job is to confirm need before a truck moves.
## Activated by one message
Because roles were assigned in advance, activation was a single message rather than a day of coordination calls. The network has since been adopted by two neighbouring districts.
replicate: Assign roles before the crisis, not during
Include verification volunteers in the roster
One activation message, no coordination calls
